newsitem.title: UK: Unilever boss attacks UK's Euro-sceptics.
newsitem.headline: Unilever boss attacks UK's Euro-sceptics.

text.p: Niall Fitzgerald, chairman of food to detergent giant Unilever Plc, on Wednesday called on the British government to embrace the European Union and condemned the body of so-called Eurosceptic politicians.

"The minority of more or less honest opponents of Europe have been joined by a much more dangerous grouping of sceptics who pretend that we can have our cake and eat it," he said in a speech to the Royal Institute of International Affairs.
"Such sceptics are searching for a means whereby Britain could continue to enjoy the benefits of the single market while minimising and perhaps escaping the wider commitments of the Union."
"These advocates should have the honesty to spell out what they mean -- closer examination reveals that their pet remedies are not as attractive as they might appear."
As a big pan-European company, Unilever would have to adapt radically if Britain opted out of Europe. Its Merseyside plant for instance, which makes toilet soaps, may have to relocate.

"Britain must not take its access to the single market for granted. The single market is Europe's greatest achievement to date; British business benefits enormously from it. This achievement and this benefit should not be put at risk."
